background_story: Lance was a brilliant geneticist who had spent his entire career studying the intricacies of cell division. His fascination with the process led him to investigate a rare occurrence known as nondisjunction, where a pair of chromosomes fails to separate properly during meiosis. Lance's research focused on understanding the causes and consequences of this phenomenon, which can lead to genetic disorders such as Down syndrome. His tireless efforts in the lab eventually led to a groundbreaking discovery, shedding new light on the mechanisms underlying nondisjunction. Lance's work has far-reaching implications for the field of genetics and has the potential to improve diagnosis and treatment of related disorders. His dedication to unlocking the secrets of nondisjunction has earned him recognition as a leading expert in his field.
